rules.title: CMMC applies to DoD contracts and subcontracts where you will handle FCI or CUI on your own systems
rules.plain_english: The CMMC program covers every DoD prime contractor and subcontractor that will process, store or transmit Federal Contract Information (FCI) or Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) on its own unclassified information systems while performing the DoD contract, commercial buys included, but not buys only for commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) items, and not federal systems a contractor runs on the government's behalf. 32 CFR 170.3(c) words the reach as solicitations and contracts 'valued at greater than the micro-purchase threshold' ($2,000 for Davis-Bacon construction, $15,000 otherwise), but the DFARS clause prescription (204.7504) states no dollar limit, so do not treat a small contract as outside CMMC: if the solicitation includes DFARS 252.204-7021, it applies. During Phases 1-3 the phase rules decide which contracts get it, and DoD may waive it for a procurement in advance; a waiver leaves every other cybersecurity requirement in place.

rules.title: CMMC phase-in: Phase 1 from Nov. 10, 2025, Phase 2 from Nov. 10, 2026, Phase 3 from Nov. 10, 2027, full implementation from Nov. 10, 2028
rules.plain_english: DoD is phasing CMMC into solicitations in four one-year steps. Phase 1 began when the DFARS CMMC acquisition rule took effect on November 10, 2025: DoD intends to require Level 1 (Self) or Level 2 (Self) as a condition of award, and may require Level 2 (C3PAO) instead. Phase 2 (from November 10, 2026) adds Level 2 (C3PAO) as a condition of award for applicable contracts (DoD may delay it to an option period) and may add Level 3 (DIBCAC). Phase 3 (from November 10, 2027): Level 2 (C3PAO) for all applicable contracts at award and for options on contracts awarded after the effective date, and Level 3 (DIBCAC) for all applicable contracts. Phase 4 (from November 10, 2028): CMMC in all applicable DoD solicitations and contracts, including option periods on contracts awarded earlier. These are DoD's stated intentions; the level written into your solicitation is the one that binds you.

rules.plain_english: The DFARS CMMC clause (252.204-7021) and its solicitation notice (252.204-7025) go into DoD solicitations, contracts and orders, commercial buys included and COTS-only buys excluded. rules.title: CMMC Level 1 = the 15 basic safeguarding requirements of FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)
rules.plain_english: Level 1 protects FCI and consists of exactly the 15 basic safeguarding requirements listed in FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)(i)-(xv): access control, identification and authentication, media sanitization, physical protection, boundary protection and system integrity (patching, malware protection and scans). They are self-assessed with the NIST SP 800-171A objectives that 32 CFR 170.15 maps to each one, reading 'FCI' wherever an objective says 'CUI'.

requirements: (i) limit system access to authorized users, processes acting for them, and devices
(ii) limit system access to the transactions and functions authorized users may execute
(iii) verify and control/limit connections to and use of external information systems
(iv) control information posted or processed on publicly accessible systems
(v) identify users, processes acting for users, and devices
(vi) authenticate users, processes or devices before allowing access
(vii) sanitize or destroy media containing FCI before disposal or reuse
(viii) limit physical access to systems, equipment and operating environments to authorized individuals
(ix) escort visitors and monitor visitor activity, keep physical access audit logs, control physical access devices
(x) monitor, control and protect communications at external and key internal boundaries
(xi) put publicly accessible system components on subnetworks separated from internal networks
(xii) identify, report and correct information and system flaws in a timely manner
(xiii) provide protection from malicious code at appropriate locations
(xiv) update malicious code protection when new releases are available
(xv) run periodic system scans and real-time scans of files from external sources

rules.title: CMMC Level 3 = 24 selected NIST SP 800-172 requirements, assessed by DCMA DIBCAC after a Final Level 2 (C3PAO)
rules.plain_english: DoD generally reserves Level 3 for solicitations supporting its most critical programs and technologies. It adds 24 enhanced requirements selected from NIST SP 800-172 (February 2021) with DoD-set parameters, such as a 24/7 security operations center, an incident response team deployable within 24 hours and penetration testing at least annually. Only DCMA DIBCAC performs Level 3 assessments, and only for systems that already hold a Final Level 2 (C3PAO) status; both the Level 3 and the Level 2 (C3PAO) assessment are repeated every three years. Each Level 3 requirement is worth 1 point.

rules.title: Level 2 (Self): self-assess against all 110 requirements every 3 years, post the score in SPRS, affirm yearly
rules.plain_english: For Level 2 (Self) you assess your own CUI systems against all Level 2 requirements with NIST SP 800-171A, score them with the CMMC scoring method and enter the results in SPRS (including the overall score, e.g. 105 out of 110, and any POA&M). A score of 110 gives Final Level 2 (Self); a qualifying POA&M gives Conditional Level 2 (Self). Repeat every three years, have the Affirming Official affirm at each assessment and every year, and keep the evidence for 6 years. Level 2 (Self) also satisfies Level 1 (Self) for the same scope. DoD may still audit you (DCMA DIBCAC), and those results override your self-assessment.

rules.title: Conditional status: a POA&M is allowed only at Levels 2 and 3, with a score of at least 80%, closed out within 180 days
rules.plain_english: A plan of action and milestones (POA&M) is never allowed at Level 1. At Level 2 you can get a Conditional status only if your score divided by 110 is at least 0.8 (a score of 88 or more), every POA&M item is worth 1 point (except SC.L2-3.13.11 encryption that is not FIPS-validated, worth 3), and none of six listed requirements (external connections, public information, the system security plan, visitor escort, physical access logs, physical access devices) is on the POA&M. At Level 3 the score must be at least 80% of the 24 requirements (20 or more) and seven listed requirements may not be on the POA&M. All NOT MET items must be fixed and confirmed by a closeout assessment within 180 days of the Conditional CMMC Status Date, or the status expires; then contract remedies apply and you cannot win new awards at that level until you get a new status.

rules.title: Level 2 scoring: start at 110 and subtract 5, 3 or 1 point for each requirement NOT MET; the score can go negative
rules.plain_english: A Level 2 assessment starts at the maximum score (the number of Level 2 requirements, 110) and subtracts each NOT MET requirement's value: 5 points for requirements whose absence could lead to significant exploitation or CUI exfiltration, 3 for a specific and confined effect, 1 for a limited or indirect effect. Multi-factor authentication only for remote and privileged users costs 3 instead of 5; encryption that is not FIPS-validated costs 3 instead of 5. The score can be negative. A requirement that does not apply (N/A) counts as MET. Without an up-to-date system security plan the assessment cannot be completed. At Level 3 each requirement is worth 1 point.
